diagnostic_evidence.quote:
can be continuously extended to a
continuous mapping $\gamma_{1}:H^{1}\left(  \omega,\Delta\right)  \rightarrow
H^{-1/2}\left(  \Gamma\right)  $

issues.failure_explanation: Two displays earlier gamma_1 is defined only on H^1(omega,Delta), so the condition 'gamma_1 v in H^{-1/2}(Gamma)' is not meaningful for a general v in H^1(omega). Read on H^1(omega,Delta) the condition is automatic (gamma_1 maps into H^{-1/2}), so the set coincides with H^1(omega,Delta), on which the prescribed norm, which uses ||gamma_1 v||_{L^2(Gamma)}, is not finite. The membership condition (H^{-1/2} trace) and the norm (L^2 trace) are incompatible, so the space is not well-defined as a normed space.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the space as {v in H^1(omega,Delta) : gamma_1 v in H^{-1/2}(Gamma)} with norm sqrt(||v||^2_{H^1}+||gamma_1 v||^2_{H^{-1/2}}) (consistent with the right-hand side of (eqn:C_F) and with CorTrace), or alternatively require gamma_1 v in L^2(Gamma) in the definition to match the stated L^2 norm and add the corresponding trace-regularity hypothesis where the space is invoked.
issues.overall_effect: The hypothesis space H^1(Omega,S_R) of Theorem thm:C_Friedrich and the ambient space used in its proof are ambiguous. The two natural corrections lead to different meanings; under the L^2-trace reading, the application to the functions in Corollary CorTrace (whose normal trace is only known to lie in H^{-1/2}) would not be justified.
issues.title: Trace space H^1(omega,Gamma) is ill-defined (H^{-1/2} condition vs L^2 norm, gamma_1 undefined on H^1)
issues.why_classification: A local definitional correction with a standard choice of trace regularity; no argument depends on the inconsistent reading beyond what is repaired locally, and all results retain their content.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper works with complex-valued data and solutions throughout (complex wavenumbers, sesquilinear pairings). A pointwise real inequality u(r xi) - b log r <= C r^{-1} (no modulus) is not defined for complex u, and with b real the condition excludes the actual solutions: for g = i the Green solution is u(r xi) = i log r / log R (cf. (uhatlog)), and |u - b log r| = |log r| |i/log R - b| >= (log r)/log R, which is not <= C r^{-1} for any real b. Hence IC_0^Green for n=2 as written is ill-defined and too restrictive, and the existence claim of Proposition PropProblems.2b fails literally for complex data.

failure_location.quote:
\exists b\in\mathbb{R}\qquad u\left(  r\xi\right)  -b\log r\leq Cr^{-1}
\quad\text{as }r\rightarrow\infty\text{ uniformly in }\xi\in S_{1}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the condition by: there exists b in C with |u(r xi) - b log r| <= C r^{-1} uniformly in xi in S_1. Both corrections are forced by the complex-valued setting and are standard; all subsequent statements then hold as written.
issues.overall_effect: The 2D logarithmic radiation condition is meaningless as stated for complex solutions; Proposition PropProblems.2b and the operators S_log and DtN^log built on it (hence also Lemma lem:two dimensions) are unreliable for complex data until the condition is corrected.
issues.title: 2D logarithmic radiation condition (SRCd) ill-defined for complex solutions (real b, missing modulus)
issues.why_classification: The two corrections (b complex, modulus) are forced and standard; once made, Proposition PropProblems.2b and Lemma lem:two dimensions hold exactly as stated, with no change to any argument.

issues.failure_explanation: Since n-1 = 2 nu + 1, direct evaluation gives F^2_{m,j} = R^{2m+4 nu} int_R^d r^{1-2(m+nu)} dr: F^2 = (d^2-R^2)/2 for m+nu=0 (not log(d/R)), F^2 = R^{2 nu+2} log(d/R) for m+nu=1 (not R^{2 nu}/2), and F^2 <= R^{2 nu+2}/(2(m+nu-1)) for m+nu >= 2; the tabulated F^2 values (and analogously the G^2 case split, including the undefined log(d/r)) use a wrong power of r. Moreover H^2_{m,j} uses m^2 where the angular energy requires the Laplace-Beltrami eigenvalue lambda_m = m(m+n-2). Consequently the uniform bound max{F^2,G^2,H^2} <= (d/R)^4 R^{2 nu}(1+R^2)(m+2 nu)(nu+2) fails for the constant mode m=nu=0 (right-hand side 0 while F^2 = (d^2-R^2)/2 > 0), and the penultimate display bounding the H^1 norm by (sum (m+2 nu)|g_hat|^2)^{1/2} is literally false for constant data in n=2: the left side is positive while the sum vanishes.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Recompute the integrals correctly (e.g., F^2=(d^2-R^2)/2 for m+nu=0), use lambda_m = m(m+n-2) in place of m^2 in H^2, and estimate with the weight (1+m+2 nu) instead of (m+2 nu); then sum (1+m+2 nu)|g_hat_{m,j}|^2 <= (1+2 nu) sum (1+m)|g_hat|^2 is controlled by ||g||^2_{H^{1/2}(S_R)}, which also controls the constant mode. The final continuity statement and the form of its constant are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed estimates in the appendix proof of Proposition PropProblems.2a are incorrect, and the final weighted estimate has a gap for the two-dimensional constant mode. The conclusion itself (continuity of g -> u from H^{1/2}(S_R) to H^1_loc(B_R^+), hence Proposition PropProblems.2a) remains correct.
issues.title: Miscomputed radial mode integrals and uncontrolled 2D constant mode in the appendix proof of Proposition PropProblems.2a
issues.why_classification: Only the displayed computations and the mode weight need routine correction; the result and its constant structure are unchanged and no other result depends on the erroneous formulas.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
This proof considers the unit disc $S_{1}$ ($R=1$) and the general case $R>0$
follows from the scaling of the norms and the arising constants then also depend
on $R$.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof establishes the bound for R=1 and invokes scaling, but the DtN eigenvalues scale like 1/R (DtN_R(s) g = R^{-1}[DtN_1(sR) g_hat] o (./R); cf. z_{m,nu}(0)=-(m+2 nu) on S_R giving the eigenvalue -(m+2 nu)/R). Hence scaling yields only the R-dependent lower bound ((n-1)/(2R)) ||g||^2, not the stated R-independent (n-2)/2 ||g||^2. The stated bound is false for large R: for n=3, s=0, R=3, g identically 1, DtN(0)1 = -1/3, so -Re<DtN(0)1,1> = (1/3)|S_3| = 12 pi < 18 pi = ((n-2)/2)||1||^2_{L^2(S_3)}. (More generally it fails for R > (n-1)/(n-2), using large imaginary wavenumbers where -Re z_{m,nu} approaches nu+1/2.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State item (iii) with the sharp R-dependent lower constant: ((n-1)/(2R)) ||g||^2_{L^2(S_R)} <= -Re<DtN(s)g,g> for n >= 3 (and 0 for n=2), exactly what the R=1 proof plus scaling yields. The theorem already permits R-dependent constants, so this is consistent with its framing.
issues.overall_effect: Item (iii) of Theorem thm:DtN as stated is false for R > 2 in any dimension n >= 3 (e.g., n=3, R=3, s=0, constant data). The definiteness content (positivity of -Re<DtN(s)g,g> for n >= 3) and every downstream use survive: Theorem thm:C_Friedrich uses only positivity of the lower constant.
issues.title: Lower coercivity bound in Theorem thm:DtN(iii) is not R-independent: false for large R
issues.why_classification: The repair is a single explicit constant (inserting the factor 1/R) already implicit in the paper's own scaling argument; the coercivity/definiteness content, the regime (all R>0, n>=3), and all dependent results are preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: For n=2 the m=0 spectral coefficient only obeys -+Im z_{0,0}(s) <= c_2 + |Im s| (Theorem thm:zmn(iii)), not <= C |Im s|: as k downarrow 0, -Im z_{0,0}(i k) = 2/(pi M_0^2(k)) ~ (pi/2)/ln^2(k/2), which exceeds C k for small k. Thus for constant g = Y_{0,1} and small imaginary s the displayed intermediate bound 0 < -+Im<DtN(s)g,g> <= C(n)|Im s| ||g||^2_{L^2(S_1)} is false in two dimensions. The theorem's stated item (iv), with upper bound C(n)||g||^2_{H^{1/2},s}, is nevertheless valid since c_2 ||g||^2_{L^2} is controlled by ||g||^2_{H^{1/2},s}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the display by the correct consequence of Theorem thm:zmn(iii): -+Im<DtN(s)g,g> <= c_2 |g_hat_{0,1}|^2 + |Im s| ||g||^2_{L^2(S_1)} <= C(n)||g||^2_{H^{1/2}(S_1),s}, which is exactly the stated item (iv).
issues.overall_effect: An intermediate display in the proof of Theorem thm:DtN is false for n=2; item (iv) of the theorem is unaffected, and no other claim in the paper uses the false display.
issues.title: Proof of Theorem thm:DtN claims an |Im s|-linear imaginary bound that is false in two dimensions
issues.why_classification: The false display is repaired immediately from Theorem thm:zmn(iii), the stated result is unchanged, and nothing else depends on it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Assume for a contradiction to (\ref{eqn:C_F}) that there exists a sequence
$(v_{k})_{k\in\mathbb{N}}\subset H$ with $\left\Vert v_{k}\right\Vert
_{L^{2}\left(  \Omega\right)  }=1$ for all $k\in\mathbb{N}$ and $\Vert\nabla
v_{k}\Vert_{L^{2}\left(  \Omega\right)  }+\left\Vert \partial_{r}
v_{k}\right\Vert _{L^{2}\left(  S_{R}\right)  }\rightarrow0$ as $k\rightarrow
\infty$.

Because $u\in H$, there exists $s\in\mathbb{C}_{\geq0}$ with
$\operatorname*{DtN}\left(  s\right)    u  =\partial_{r}u$.

issues.failure_explanation: Two defects in the compactness argument. (i) Negation of (eqn:C_F) only yields a normalized sequence with ||nabla v_k||_{L^2} + ||partial_r v_k||_{H^{-1/2}(S_R)} -> 0; the proof assumes the stronger ||partial_r v_k||_{L^2(S_R)} -> 0, which is not available and is precisely what makes the sequence bounded in the norm of H (which contains ||gamma_1 v||_{L^2}). (ii) The asserted completeness of H = union over z in C_{>=0} of {v : partial_r v = DtN(z) v} is false: continuity of s -> DtN(s) does not close the union over unbounded z. Counterexample: on S_1 take constant traces g_k = 1/k and z_k = k; by the paper's own asymptotic (m - z_{m,nu}(s) - s -> mu + 1/2), DtN(k) g_k = z_{0,nu}(k)/k -> -1, so one can choose v_k in H converging in H^1(Omega,S_1) to v with v|_{S_1}=0 but partial_r v = -1, while DtN(z)(v|_{S_1}) = 0 for every z; hence v is not in H. Therefore the weak limit u need not belong to H and the concluding step ('Because u in H, there exists s ...') is unjustified.

failure_location.quote:
(The completeness of $H$ follows from the continuity of the
$\operatorname*{DtN}\left(  s\right)  $ operator by \Cref{thm:DtN}.)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Drop the completeness claim and the L^2 assumption: from the negation of (eqn:C_F), ||nabla v_k||_{L^2} -> 0 and ||partial_r v_k||_{H^{-1/2}(S_R)} -> 0; the weak H^1-limit u is constant with ||u||_{L^2}=1, and Theorem thm:DtN(iii) applied to v_k|_{S_R} with partial_r v_k = DtN(z_k) v_k gives ((n-2)/2)||v_k||^2_{L^2(S_R)} <= |<partial_r v_k, v_k>| <= ||partial_r v_k||_{H^{-1/2}} ||v_k||_{H^{1/2}(S_R)} -> 0, so u has zero trace on S_R, hence u = 0, a contradiction.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of Theorem thm:C_Friedrich is incomplete as written: it relies on a false completeness assertion and on an assumption stronger than the negation of (eqn:C_F) provides. The statement of Theorem thm:C_Friedrich is nonetheless true, and Corollary CorTrace, whose proof applies it, depends on the same gap.
issues.title: Proof of Theorem thm:C_Friedrich: unjustified L^2(S_R) convergence assumption and false completeness of H
issues.why_classification: More than a local patch: the proof explicitly invokes a false completeness claim and a stronger convergence than the negation of (eqn:C_F) yields, so the contradiction argument must be restructured. The repair is however contained in the same proof, uses only Theorem thm:DtN(iii), and loses no content: the theorem and Corollary CorTrace survive unchanged.
